usage.heading: Usage
usage.description: Metered usage, and the billing periods rated from it. Windows are half-open and UTC: everything from the first date up to, but not including, the second.

common.requestFailed: The request failed, and said nothing about why.
common.subject: Subject

window.bothRequired: Both dates are required, as YYYY-MM-DD.
window.endsBeforeStart: The window ends before it starts.
window.noWidth: That window has no width, so it would always total nothing. `To` is exclusive, so it must be the day AFTER the last one you want.

ingestion.title: Ingestion
ingestion.description: What this instance of the plugin is doing with the events it is given.

rates.emptyTitle: The rate card prices no meters
rates.emptyBody: A rate card with no meters rates every period at zero. That is a valid answer and a surprising invoice, so it is worth checking that it was the intended one.

meters.title: Meters
meters.descriptionAll: What every subject together consumed in the chosen window, meter by meter.
meters.descriptionSubject: What "{{subject}}" consumed in the chosen window, meter by meter.
meters.emptyBody: This installation has no rate card, so the plugin does not know which meter names exist - it records whatever a producer sends it. Type a meter name above to ask the log what it holds for that one.

periods.title: Billing periods
periods.descriptionAll: Newest window first. A period is closed when, and only when, it has a frozen result. The dates above do not filter this list.
periods.descriptionSubject: Periods for "{{subject}}", newest window first. A period is closed when, and only when, it has a frozen result. The dates above do not filter this list.
periods.truncated_one: Showing the first {{count}}, which is as many as this panel asks for. There are very likely more: narrow by subject or by status to reach them.
periods.truncated_other: Showing the first {{count}}, which is as many as this panel asks for. There are very likely more: narrow by subject or by status to reach them.
periods.emptyBody: This is the expected state on a new installation, and it is not a fault. The plugin does not create periods, because only the application knows what a billing cycle is here - whether it is a calendar month, thirty days from the day someone signed up, or something else. Open one with `POST /admin/usage/periods`, from a job of your own, and it will appear in this list.
periods.emptyFilteredBody: Clear the subject, or set the status back to any, to see whether there are periods that do not match rather than none at all.

events.title: Events
events.descriptionAll: {{meter}}, every subject, oldest first, from {{from}} up to {{to}}.
events.descriptionSubject: {{meter}} for {{subject}}, oldest first, from {{from}} up to {{to}}.
events.emptyBody: Nothing was recorded on this meter in the window named above. A meter that has never been written to and a meter whose usage falls outside the window look the same from here, so widening the window is the first thing to try.
events.shownAll_one: {{shown}} shown, which is all of them.
events.shownAll_other: {{shown}} shown, which is all of them.

period.title: Billing period
period.statusUnknown: Whether this period can be closed is not known: reading the plugin's status failed. {{error}}

confirm.description: This rates {{subject}} over {{from}} to {{to}} against the current rate card and freezes the answer. It is safe to retry and cannot bill the same period twice, but the frozen result does not move afterwards.
confirm.title: Close this period?

period.noResultBody: This period is open, which means it has not been billed. That is a different thing from a result whose total is zero: an open period says do not bill this yet, while a closed one worth nothing says it provably came to nothing.

accrued.heading: Accrued so far, over this period's own boundaries

ingestion.instance: These counts are for the instance that served this request, not the deployment.
ingestion.flushFailed_one: The "{{sink}}" sink said: {{error}}. {{count}} event waiting. Until a flush succeeds, usage is only in memory.
ingestion.flushFailed_other: The "{{sink}}" sink said: {{error}}. {{count}} events waiting. Until a flush succeeds, usage is only in memory.
ingestion.immediateHeadline: Writing each event as it arrives
ingestion.immediateDetail: Every event is written to the "{{sink}}" sink as it arrives, so nothing buffers and there is no flush to be behind on.
ingestion.neverFlushed_one: {{count}} event waiting, oldest {{oldest}}, and nothing has been flushed to "{{sink}}" yet. Flushes run every {{interval}}, or sooner at {{batchSize}} events. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)
ingestion.neverFlushed_other: {{count}} events waiting, oldest {{oldest}}, and nothing has been flushed to "{{sink}}" yet. Flushes run every {{interval}}, or sooner at {{batchSize}} events. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)
ingestion.recordingBuffered_one: {{count}} event waiting, oldest {{oldest}}. Last flush to "{{sink}}" at {{lastFlush}}. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)
ingestion.recordingBuffered_other: {{count}} events waiting, oldest {{oldest}}. Last flush to "{{sink}}" at {{lastFlush}}. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)
ingestion.recordingIdleDetail: Nothing waiting. The last flush to "{{sink}}" was at {{lastFlush}}. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)
ingestion.idleDetail: Nothing is buffered and this instance has not flushed anything. That is what a healthy plugin with no producer looks like, and also what a broken producer looks like. $t(usage.verdicts.ingestion.instance)

rateCard.meteringOnlyDetail: No rate card is configured, so this installation meters without pricing. Periods can be opened and read, but not closed.
rateCard.rated_one: {{count}} meter priced in {{currency}}. A period is held open for {{delay}} after it ends before it can be closed.
rateCard.rated_other: {{count}} meters priced in {{currency}}. A period is held open for {{delay}} after it ends before it can be closed.

closability.closed: Closed at {{closedAt}}. The frozen result is what was billed, and closing again would return it unchanged rather than bill twice.
closability.unknown: Still reading the rate card, so whether this period can be closed is not known yet.
closability.noRateCard: There is no rate card, so there is nothing to rate this period against. Configure `billing` in the plugin options before closing it.
closability.tooEarly: Not closable until {{closableAt}}. The window ends at {{endsAt}}.
closability.tooEarlyWithHold: Not closable until {{closableAt}}. The window ends at {{endsAt}}, and it is held open for a further {{delay}} so events still in a buffer can land.
closability.closable: The window is over. Closing rates it against the rate card and freezes the answer; it is safe to retry and cannot bill twice.

verification.unchanged: The frozen result has not been rewritten, and will not be.
verification.matchesDetail: Rated again from the log, this period still comes to {{total}} and the same digest. The evidence behind the invoice has not moved.
verification.noneMovedDetail: No meter's quantity or amount has moved, and the digest still differs. A digest covers the evidence and not only the total: the instants a line spans, and the snapshot it was rated from, are inside it. Events that cancel out, or arrive with a quantity of zero, look exactly like this. $t(usage.verdicts.verification.unchanged)
verification.differ_one: {{moved}} of {{count}} meter differs. The log now totals {{recomputed}} against the {{stored}} that was billed, a difference of {{delta}}. $t(usage.verdicts.verification.unchanged)
verification.differ_other: {{moved}} of {{count}} meters differ. The log now totals {{recomputed}} against the {{stored}} that was billed, a difference of {{delta}}. $t(usage.verdicts.verification.unchanged)
